newsitem.title: ITALY: Sudan's leader slams Washington on U.N. sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Sudan's leader slams Washington on U.N. sanctions.

text.p: Sudan's President Omar Hassan Al-Bashir attacked the United States on Thursday, saying Washington was behind U.N. sanctions against his country.

Bashir, who is in Rome for a U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit, told a news conference there was no evidence that Sudan was involved in an assassination attempt against Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak that led to the sanctions.
He said the limited embargo was part of the "logic of American hegemony".
"Perhaps what is happening in Rwanda, Burundi and Zaire is not enough for the United States. Maybe they would like us to join this chain of tragedies and massacres," Bashir said.

The United States has labelled Sudan's Islamist government "terrorist". Most of the African state's neighbours accuse it of harbouring and training rebels trying to overthrow their more secular regimes.

The United Nations has slapped limited travel and diplomatic sanctions on Sudan for failing to extradite to Egypt or Ethiopia three gunmen accused of trying to kill Mubarak in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa in June 1995.

The Security Council on August 16 also imposed an air embargo on Sudan but delayed putting it into effect for at least three months depending on a U.N. report on whether Khartoum was complying with the council's demands.
Sudan says the men are not within its borders and that there is no concrete evidence that it harbours the suspects.
